subtopics.title: Basic Operations, Concepts, and Keyboarding (1 of 6)

outcomes.text: Identify the basic components of the computing device, whether a computer, laptop, or hand-held device (e.g., monitor/screen, keyboard, mouse/trackpad, ports, power source).
Turn on/off a computing device and follow appropriate procedures to access the device.
Use a mouse or trackpad to manipulate shapes and icons; navigate within applications (e.g., click on hyperlinks, radio buttons, check boxes, use scroll bars).
Use desktop icons, windows, and menus to open, minimize, and close applications or files.
Use shortcuts and command functions to operate the computer or applications (e.g., Command-P, Command-C, Command-V, Command-Z, Ctrl-Alt- Delete, etc.).

subtopics.title: Basic Operations, Concepts, and Keyboarding (2 of 6)

outcomes.text: Use gestures to navigate hand-held devices (e.g., swipe-left, swipe-right, pinch, etc.).
Locate and utilize accessibility features.
Use application help functions and online resources to solve basic operational issues (e.g., connecting to Bluetooth devices, finding a printer, internet connectivity) independently.
Use proper posture and ergonomics while using a computing device, including hand-held devices.
Locate and use the correct finger/hand for the space bar, return/enter, and shift key.

subtopics.title: Basic Operations, Concepts, and Keyboarding (3 of 6)

outcomes.text: Locate and use letter and number keys with correct left and right hand placement (home row).
Learn to use special characters as needed (e.g., accents, tilde).
Use a calendar, task manager, or other tools to organize oneself as well as manage projects.
Use graphic organizers, brainstorming applications, or other digital tools to gather and organize information (e.g., a Jamboard, online drawing tool, online slides).
Understand all rules and guidelines in the school's Acceptable Use Policy.

subtopics.title: Basic Operations, Concepts, and Keyboarding (4 of 6)

outcomes.text: Understand Fair Use guidelines and their application to all forms of work.
Demonstrate understanding of the difference between cloud computing vs. software applications for file storage/management.
Use login credentials to access network devices, accounts, file servers, and cloud services.
Name files with appropriate file names and understand where files are being saved.
Create, save, edit, copy, and rename files and folders to organize files and materials.

subtopics.title: Basic Operations, Concepts, and Keyboarding (5 of 6)

outcomes.text: Delete and recover deleted files and folders and permanently delete files.
Retrieve previous file versions/access revision history for files located in cloud services.
Download, upload, attach files/folders via the web, email, or cloud services.
Compress files and folders via the web, email, or cloud services.
Use search tools to locate files and applications.

subtopics.title: Basic Operations, Concepts, and Keyboarding (6 of 6)

outcomes.text: Associate document extensions with appropriate file types.

subtopics.title: Innovative Designer - Students use a variety of technologies within a design process to identify and solve problems by creating new, useful or imaginative solutions. Students:

outcomes.text: Know and use a deliberate design process for generating ideas, testing theories, creating innovative artifacts or solving authentic problems.
Select and use digital tools to plan and manage a design process that considers design constraints and calculated risks.
Develop, test and refine prototypes as part of a cyclical design process.
Exhibit a tolerance for ambiguity, perseverance and the capacity to work with open-ended problems.

units.title: Computational Thinker - Students develop and employ strategies for understanding and solving problems in ways that leverage the power of technological methods to develop and test solutions. Students:

topics.title: Computational Thinker - Students develop and employ strategies for understanding and solving problems in ways that leverage the power of technological methods to develop and test solutions. Students:

subtopics.title: Computational Thinker - Students develop and employ strategies for understanding and solving problems in ways that leverage the power of technological methods to develop and test solutions. Students:

outcomes.text: Formulate problem definitions suited for technology assisted methods such as data analysis, abstract models and algorithmic thinking in exploring and finding solutions.
Collect data or identify relevant data sets, use digital tools to analyze them, and represent data in various ways to facilitate problem-solving and decision-making.
Break problems into component parts, extract key information, and develop descriptive models to understand complex systems or facilitate problem-solving.
Understand how automation works and use algorithmic thinking to develop a sequence of steps to create and test automated solutions.

topics.title: Creative Communicator - Students communicate clearly and express themselves creatively for a variety of purposes using the platforms, tools, styles, formats and digital media appropriate to their goals. Students:

subtopics.title: Creative Communicator - Students communicate clearly and express themselves creatively for a variety of purposes using the platforms, tools, styles, formats and digital media appropriate to their goals. Students:

outcomes.text: Choose the appropriate platforms and tools for meeting the desired objectives of their creation or communication.
Create original works or responsibly repurpose or remix digital resources into new creations.
Communicate complex ideas clearly and effectively by creating or using a variety of digital objects such as visualizations, models or simulations.
Publish or present content that customizes the message and medium for their intended audiences.

subtopics.title: Global Collaborator - Students use digital tools to broaden their perspectives and enrich their learning by collaborating with others and working effectively in teams locally and globally. Students:

outcomes.text: Use digital tools to connect with learners from a variety of backgrounds and cultures, engaging with them in ways that broaden mutual understanding and learning.
Use collaborative technologies to work with others, including peers, experts or community members, to examine issues and problems from multiple viewpoints.
Contribute constructively to project teams, assuming various roles and responsibilities to work effectively toward a common goal.
Explore local and global issues and use collaborative technologies to work with others to investigate solutions.
